chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is an old, elderly man or sick, fearing the crowding and pressing of the people, who enters into Ihram for Hajj and departs to Mina before the Day of Tarwiyah. He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Does a healthy man depart seeking a place and rest in that place?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Does he hasten by one day?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By two days?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'By three?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'More than that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day pilgrims traditionally depart for Mina
key_terms.يَتَرَوَّحُ: To rest or settle in a place
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: Enters into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj

ai.seo_question: When should healthy pilgrims depart for Mina during Hajj, and can the elderly leave early?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'Nuzul Mina' by distinguishing between the concession for the elderly and sick to leave early to avoid 'zigam' (crowding) and the general rule for healthy pilgrims. It establishes that while healthy individuals must wait until the Day of Tarwiyah (8th Dhul-Hijjah), they are permitted to hasten their departure by one, two, or three days, but not more, reflecting the practical balance between ritual timing and logistical ease in Shia jurisprudence. The dialogue highlights the Imam's precise delineation of these temporal boundaries, which remains a key reference for determining the validity of the Mina stay during Hajj.
